title: You can be doing everything for God…
paragraphs:
You can be doing everything for God…
and still be far from Him.
Let that sit.

Because Martha wasn’t sinning in the way we expect.
No rebellion.
No scandal.
No obvious failure.
Just… distraction dressed as devotion.
And that’s what makes this dangerous.
She was serving Jesus—yet missing Jesus.
Read that again.

Some of us don’t walk away from God.
We just get so busy “doing for Him” that we slowly stop being with Him.
And no one notices.

Not your church.
Not your leaders.
Not even your family.
But your soul does.
Luke tells us that Martha was “distracted with much serving” (Luke 10:40), and that word distracted carries the weight of being pulled apart, dragged in different directions.

Not evil.
Just divided.
And here’s the uncomfortable question:
When was the last time you sat with God… without rushing Him?

Not praying while scrolling.
Not worshipping while thinking about your to-do list.
Not reading Scripture just to check a box.

I mean still.
Present.
Undivided.
Or have you been calling your busyness “faithfulness”?
Because here’s the truth we don’t say out loud:
Some of us hide behind ministry so we don’t have to deal with our hearts.

We serve more…
so we don’t have to surrender more.

We stay active…
so we don’t have to get honest.

We fill our schedules…
so we don’t have to face the silence where God speaks.
And Jesus doesn’t ignore it.
He gently confronts it.
“Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is necessary.” (Luke 10:41–42)
He says her name twice.

Not to shame her.
To reach her.
That’s grace.
Because the problem was never her service.
It was her soul.
A heart that forgot that presence comes before performance.
This is where it gets personal.

You can preach and still be prayerless.
You can lead and still be lost inside.
You can sing about Him and still feel distant from Him.
That’s the silent struggle no one posts about.

Spiritual fatigue.
Delayed obedience.
Hidden pride that whispers, “God must be pleased with me—I’m doing so much.”
But Scripture cuts through that illusion.
Isaiah 29:13 says, “These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.”
That’s not atheism.
That’s religious distance.
That’s Martha.
That’s us… sometimes.
AHA REVELATION:
God is not impressed by what you do for Him if it replaces being with Him.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:
If your service is increasing but your intimacy is decreasing… you are not growing—you are drifting.
And here’s the bold truth:

God doesn’t need your performance.
He wants your presence.
That’s where everything changes.
Because Mary chose to sit.

Not because she was lazy.
But because she understood something deeper.
Jesus said she chose “the good portion” (Luke 10:42).
In Jewish language, “portion” often refers to inheritance.

In other words—
Mary chose Him as her reward.

Not the task.
Not the recognition.
Not the role.
Him.
And this is where the Gospel breaks in.
Because the truth is—we are all Martha at some point.
Trying to earn what Jesus already came to give.

We strive for approval…
but the cross already declared it.

We try to prove our worth…
but Jesus already paid for it.
Romans 5:8 says that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

Not when we got productive.
Not when we got busy.
But when we were broken.
And on that cross, Jesus didn’t say, “Do more.”
He said, “It is finished.” (John 19:30)
That means your closeness to God is not built by your activity.

It’s restored by repentance.
Received by grace.
Secured in Christ alone.
So if you’ve been distant…
Come back.

Not to a task.
Not to a system.
Not to performance.
Come back to a Person.
Jesus.

Sit again.
Listen again.
Surrender again.
You are not called to be a machine for ministry.
You are called to be a child of God.
And children don’t earn presence.
They live in it.
If this pierced your heart… don’t ignore it.
Not hype. Just truth that holds you when everything else is loud.
And next time, we’re going deeper into the moment Jesus wept—and what it reveals about the heart of God you think you know.
